title: Mechanism of Tethered Agonist Binding to an Adhesion G-Protein-Coupled Receptor
one_liner_zh: 该文用Pep-GaMD增强采样模拟研究粘附GPCR中束缚激动剂肽的构象转变与结合机制，虽涉及肽-受体互作和MD方法，但对象为蛋白-肽而非蛋白-DNA，与本课题TF-DNA互作无直接关联。
abstract: Adhesion GPCRs (ADGRs) contain a GPCR autoproteolysis-inducing (GAIN) domain that is proximal to the receptor N-terminus and undergoes autoproteolysis at a highly conserved GPCR proteolysis (GPS) site to generate the N-terminal fragment (NTF) and transmembrane C-terminal fragment (CTF). Dissociation of NTF reveals a peptide tethered agonist (TA) which is responsible for the activation of the ADGRs. The NTF-bound ADGRs contain the encrypted TA that assumes a β-strand configuration within the GAIN domain, which is markedly different from a U-shaped α-helical configuration of TA in the active cryo-EM structures of ADGRs. However, how the TA dramatically changes its configuration and binds to the ADGR CTF remains unknown. In this study, we have performed all-atom enhanced sampling simulations using a novel Peptide-Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics (Pep-GaMD) method on TA binding to the ADGRD1. The Pep-GaMD simulations captured spontaneous binding of the TA into orthosteric pocket of the ADGRD1 and its large conformational transition from the extended β strand to the U-shaped α helical configuration. We were able to identify important low-energy conformations of the TA in the binding pathway, as well as different active and inactive states of ADGRD1, in the presence and absence of the Gs protein. Therefore, our Pep-GaMD simulations have revealed dynamic mechanism of the TA binding to an ADGR, which will facilitate rational design of peptide regulators of ADGRs. TOC Graphic Peptide-Gaussian accelerated Molecular Dynamics (Pep-GaMD) simulations remarkably captured spontaneous binding of tethered agonist (TA) into the orthosteric pocket of adhesion G-protein–coupled receptor (ADGRD1) and large conformational transition of the TA from an extended β-strand to a U-shaped α-helical configuration. We were able to identify important low-energy conformations of the TA in the binding pathway and different states of the receptor from the Pep-GaMD simulations.
abstract_zh: 粘附性G蛋白偶联受体（Adhesion GPCRs, ADGRs）含有一个GPCR自蛋白水解诱导（GAIN）结构域，该结构域位于受体N末端附近，并在高度保守的GPCR蛋白水解（GPS）位点发生自蛋白水解，生成N端片段（NTF）和跨膜C端片段（CTF）。NTF的解离暴露了一个肽段束缚激动剂（TA），该激动剂负责激活ADGRs。与NTF结合的ADGRs包含加密的TA，其在GAIN结构域内呈β链构象，这与ADGRs活性冷冻电镜结构中TA的U形α螺旋构象显著不同。然而，TA如何剧烈改变其构象并绑定至ADGR CTF仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们采用一种新颖的肽段-高斯加速分子动力学（Pep-GaMD）方法，对TA与ADGRD1的结合进行了全原子增强采样模拟。Pep-GaMD模拟捕获了TA自发结合至ADGRD1的正构口袋，以及其从延伸β链到U形α螺旋构象的大规模构象转变。我们能够识别TA在结合途径中的重要低能构象，以及在有无Gs蛋白情况下ADGRD1的不同活性和非活性状态。因此，我们的Pep-GaMD模拟揭示了TA与ADGR结合的动态机制，这将有助于ADGRs肽段调节剂的合理设计。TOC图形摘要：肽段-高斯加速分子动力学（Pep-GaMD）模拟显著捕获了束缚激动剂（TA）自发结合至粘附性G蛋白偶联受体（ADGRD1）的正构口袋，以及TA从延伸β链到U形α螺旋构象的大规模构象转变。我们能够从Pep-GaMD模拟中识别TA在结合途径中的重要低能构象及受体的不同状态。
